documented_diagnosis.name: Actinic keratosis
documented_diagnosis.evidence: Clinical diagnosis by the dermatologists who collected the dataset; not biopsied (PAD-UFES-20).

teaching_points: Actinic keratoses are rough, scaly spots on long-term sun-damaged skin. They are often easier to feel than to see.
They are precancerous: a small proportion become squamous cell carcinoma.
A spot that thickens, becomes tender or grows quickly needs assessment.

look_alikes.name: Bowen disease (SCC in situ)
look_alikes.note: A larger, well-defined red scaly plaque.

look_alikes.name: Superficial basal cell carcinoma
look_alikes.note: A thin pink patch, often with a shiny, thread-like edge.

look_alikes.name: Seborrheic keratosis
look_alikes.note: Stuck-on and waxy rather than rough and red.
